title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§11 'Digression', previous page): a topological ordered set Σ = (Σ(0), Σ(1)). Σ(0) is a space and Σ(1) ⊂ Σ(0)×Σ(0) is a closed subset that is the graph of an order relation. The axioms are: (a) the target map 'but': Σ(1)→Σ(0) is a proper, finite-fibred, locally 'bordant' immersion, meaning it is locally the inclusion of a boundary face; (b) the diagonal Σ(0)→Σ(1) is an open-and-closed immersion. Σ*(1) is the complement of the diagonal (strict pairs i<j), and Σ*(n) is the space of strict chains i0<…<in. These form a presimplicial (semi-simplicial) space, with no degeneracies. For a finite totally ordered 'shape' d, Σ'(d) (=Σ*(d)) denotes the space of strict chains of type d. It is contravariant in d through restriction to subchains.

This page has two steps.

(i) Gluing (Segal) condition. Take a square of inclusions of totally ordered sets d ⊂ d'' = d∪d' ⊃ d', with δ = d∩d', which is a pushout of ordered sets. The intended case is that d and d' overlap only in the last element of d, which is the first element of d'; any order-compatible overlap works. Then the induced square Σ'(d'') → Σ'(d), Σ'(d') → Σ'(δ) is a fibre product: Σ'(d'') = Σ'(d) ×_{Σ'(δ)} Σ'(d'). In modern terms the semi-simplicial space of strict chains satisfies the Segal condition, so it is a (non-unital) category object in Top. For the nerve of a topological poset with closed graph this is automatic: chains form closed subspaces of Σ(0)^{n+1}, and fibre products carry the subspace topology.

(ii) Collapsing the earlier conditions. Grothendieck says the conditions (b),(c),(d) of the preceding numbers collapse here into a single condition of type (d). For a chain type d = (i0<…<in) of 'dimension' ≥1, consider the family of maps Σ'(d) → Σ'(i_k,i_n) → Σ'(i_n), k = 0,…,n−1. Here the φ_k = 'but' maps are bordant immersions. The next page states the condition fully: near each point, Σ*(d) embedded in Σ*({i_n}) ≅ Σ*(0) is the intersection of the bordant subspaces Σ*({i_k,i_n}) ≅ Σ*(1), and this family is transversal. The analogous statement then follows for all restriction maps Σ*(d')→Σ*(d) (diagram (34)).

Geometrically, Σ(0) is the disjoint union of the 'deployed' strata. These are manifolds with corners, one per stratum, roughly the complement of a tubular neighbourhood of the lower strata. A strict pair i<j is a boundary face of the deployed j-stratum lying over the deployed i-stratum, with the target map the face inclusion and the source map the link fibration. A chain of length n is a codimension-n corner, cut out transversally by n boundary hypersurfaces. So the page encodes the corner/face combinatorics of the 'déploiement' of a stratified space as a semi-simplicial topological poset with a transversality axiom. This is the purpose of the whole manuscript (conical neighbourhoods / unfolding of stratified spaces).
errors: The square (32) of spaces must be a fibre product (cartesian), not cocartesian. Σ' is contravariant and the arrows point from Σ'(d'') down to Σ'(δ); only the square (31) of ordered sets is cocartesian. The manuscript may well say 'cartésien'; the transcription's 'cocartésien' is doubtful.

The stated hypothesis ('δ initial segment of d, and d' containing the final element of d') is garbled as transcribed. The natural condition is that δ is a final segment of d and an initial segment of d' (typically δ = {max d} = {min d'}), so that d∪d' is totally ordered compatibly.
For a topological poset with closed graph the cartesian property (32) holds automatically. The genuine content is the transversality condition (33)/(34), not (32).
Notation drifts between Σ', Σ^0 and Σ* for the strict-chain spaces.

ideas.what: Topological poset (internal poset in Top) whose strict-chain nerve is a semi-simplicial space, used to encode the stratification index together with the geometry
ideas.modern_name: internal category/poset in spaces; semi-simplicial space satisfying the Segal condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968/1974) for category objects in spaces; in the stratified setting, Lurie (HA App. A) and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)

ideas.what: Gluing chains along a common element gives a fibre product of chain spaces (Segal condition)
Target map Σ(1)→Σ(0) as a bordant (boundary-face) immersion, with chains of length n as codimension-n corners obtained as transversal intersections of faces
ideas.modern_name: manifold with faces / ⟨n⟩-manifold; resolution of a Thom–Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners carrying an iterated fibration structure; 'unzipping'
ideas.where_published: The dévissage of stratified spaces into systems of spaces with boundary is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, without this internal-poset/transversality formalism.

ideas.what: Reduction of several compatibility axioms to a single transversality axiom on the family of face inclusions into the top-stratum deployment
ideas.modern_name: transversality of boundary hypersurfaces at corners (faces meeting like coordinate hyperplanes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes the deployed (unfolded) stratified space as a single topological poset, i.e. a category object in Top. The space of objects is the union of deployed strata; the space of strict arrows is the boundary faces, with target = face inclusion. A transversality axiom on chains makes the corner structure come out of the nerve. This anticipates the later 'unzipping' and iterated-fibration resolution formalisms (Albin–Melrose; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), which index the corner structure by the stratifying poset but do not use an internal-poset nerve in this form.
missed.quote: les conditions b c d des [n°] précédents [se résument] ici en une seule (du type d)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a compact, nerve-theoretic axiomatization of the 'resolution to manifolds with corners' of a stratified space. That could link directly to exit-path ∞-categories and to semi-simplicial/Segal descriptions of stratified spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working step in the déploiement programme only sketched in the Esquisse. The internal-topological-poset/semi-simplicial packaging with a transversal-corner axiom is a mildly notable unpublished formalization. The individual ingredients (Segal condition, manifolds with faces, transversal corners) are standard, and the analogous resolution theory was developed independently later.

After (32): likely 'est cartésien' (or 'Cette condition [est] cartésienne'), not 'cocartésien'.
The line read as '[?] les [?] compositions b c d des [?] principales' is likely 'Les conditions b c d des n° précédents se résument ici en une seule (du type d)'.
The following line is likely 'Soit d = (i_0, …, i_n) un ens. tot. ordonné de "dim" ≥ 1, Σ'(d) → Σ(d) [?], et considérons le diagramme'.
The struck phrase reads approximately 'plusieurs bordants'; the final line reads 'les φ_0, φ_1, …, φ_{n-1} sont bordantes. Supposons…'.
The margin note mentions 'diagramme (33)', so the unlabelled family of maps on this page is the diagram (33) referred to on the next page.
